A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first tight upper and lower bounds for the minimax risk for discrete distribution estimation under the KL loss.

, in the worst-case scenario of discrete distribution estimation, our upper bounds provide a convex minimization problem for finding an estimator with good worst-case performance, while our lower bounds provide a one-parameter family of estimators with near-optimal performance.
we provide a complete characterization of the minimax KL estimation problem, and the results can serve as the benchmark for the performance of any discrete distribution estimators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the entropy setting, the KL loss is not uniformly approximable by a finite-dimensional function space (e.g. polynomials) and thus requires a fundamentally different analysis.
, in the worst-case sense, the KL loss is a much harder problem than the entropy loss.
